title: Rules of a run (content/rules/<name>.json, schema v0)
description: Tracks, regional climate, weather effects and prices that a run is frozen from. Provisional: the values are starting points to calibrate in the economy simulator.

reference_power_kw.description: Power of a car with the fuel use of the track. More power burns more: 1 + 0.6 * power / reference, relative to 1.6.

condition_factor.description: How much a car in a poor condition breaks down more: the chance of a breakdown is multiplied by 1 + factor * (1 - condition), so a car in no condition at all breaks down factor + 1 times as often.

wear.description: Mileage, the condition of the parts and the service (Systemy III, point 11). A part that sits on a car wears with every kilometre by 1 / life_km of its life, faster on rough ground (rough_ppm), with the power of the car (power_exponent_ppm: wear x (power / reference power) ^ exponent) and with a booster on it (boost_ppm, for the parts of the engine). Its statistics are multiplied by stat_floor_ppm + (1 - stat_floor_ppm) x condition, and it is unserviceable under unserviceable_ppm. The condition counts in stages of stage_ppm, so that the frozen configuration of a run changes only when a part reaches the next one. A car is due for service every service.every_km; past it the performance falls by penalty_ppm_per_step for every step_km, at most max_steps steps.

life_km.description: How many kilometres a part of the slot lasts from new to worn out, on smooth ground at the reference power.

rough_ppm.description: How much faster a slot wears on gravel: 1 000 000 is as fast as on asphalt.

load_ppm_per_point.description: How much faster the parts of the engine (engine, booster, gearbox, cooling) wear for every point of the load of the engine (the sum of the engine_load of the parts on the car, never under 0): 10000 is 1% a point, so a booster of load 18 and an intercooler of -6 wear them 12% faster.

stat_floor_ppm.description: What a worn out part still gives of its statistics (the design: 0.6).

unserviceable_ppm.description: Under this condition a part is unserviceable and the car breaks down more.

repair_cost_ppm_of_price.description: What the repair of a part costs: this share of its price for the whole condition it is short of.

cost_ppm_of_income.description: What a service costs: this share of what the car earns between two services (the reward of a lap times the laps of every_km), so that it is the same share of the income on every rung of the ladder, whatever the car costs.

time_ms.description: How long a service takes the mechanic, before the level of the mechanic cuts it.

breakdown.description: How much the chance of a breakdown grows: by 1 + wear_factor x the mean wear of the parts, by 1 + overdue_factor x the share of the longest overdue of the service, and by 1 + unserviceable_factor for every unserviceable part.

tow.description: The way out for a driver who cannot pay to get a stopped car going: the tow is free, but the car waits for it and the time it waits costs more than the repair and the fuel would have.

delay_ms.description: How long the car waits before it drives again.

fuel_laps.description: Laps of fuel the tow leaves in an empty tank, enough to earn the next fuel.

stock_tires.description: Slug of the tires every car drives on until it has others. Their kind picks the column of the tire matrix.

bots.description: The rivals of the race: seven bots drive every track at lap times around the reference of the tier of the car (the fastest stock car of the tier on that track, `content/tables/bot-profiles.json`), and the place of the car among them, by its dry lap time, multiplies the reward of a lap. A bot as fast as the car is ahead of it.

offsets_ppm.description: The lap time of every bot against the reference, in ppm: -90 000 is a bot 9% quicker than the reference, 0 one that drives it, and 90 000 one 9% slower. There are as many bots as numbers, so the field is one car bigger.

reward_ppm_by_position.description: What the reward of a lap is multiplied by (ppm, 1 000 000 is none) for the first place, the second and so on, as many as the field has cars. It never rises with the place.

names.description: The names of the teams the bots are called by, none twice: a track takes as many as it has bots, in an order that is its own. They are names, not texts, so they are not translated.

car.description: Owned cars. A part of tier T can be mounted in a car whose level is at least levels_per_tier * (T - 1): tier <= 1 + floor(level / levels_per_tier).

start_level.description: The level of a car when the driver gets it.

levels_per_upgrade.description: A part can be upgraded to +N on a car whose level is at least levels_per_upgrade * (N - 1): the upgrade of a part is at most 1 + floor(level / levels_per_upgrade), and at most what its rarity allows.

xp_per_lap.description: The experience a car gets for every lap it drives, in any weather: the laps of this car are what it levels on.

xp_per_level.description: The experience from level n to level n + 1 is xp_per_level * n, so a level takes more than the one before it, and the experience to reach level n is xp_per_level * n * (n - 1) / 2.

reward_ppm_from_tier.description: What a lap pays as a share of the reward of the track, by the tier of the car (ppm, 1 000 000 is all of it): the factor of a tier is the one of the highest tier named that is at most it, and the tiers have to name tier 1. The design makes the profit of an hour a function of the rung of the car (Systemy VI), so a car of a higher tier earns more on the same track; the economy simulator checks that the best car of every level pays about what its rung asks.

mass.description: A heavier car handles and brakes worse, a lighter one better: handling and braking are multiplied by (reference_kg / mass) ^ exponent. A car of the reference mass is not touched, so the stock Rdzak stays the reference of the first track.

lag_ppm_per_point.description: The lag of a booster (1 to 10, the design) takes this much off the acceleration of the car for every point: 10000 is 1% a point. The top speed is not touched.

max_level.description: The level a car does not rise above, whatever experience it has. It has to be high enough for the highest tier.

stat_ceiling.description: The value of a statistic at which its bar in the garage is full: what the best car of the whole game is meant to reach, not what a track asks for. A car that has only just left the wreck yard stands well below it.

engines.description: The engines (Systemy II, Katalog części): a model is a layout and a displacement, and what it gives comes from the layout (kW per litre, the mass of the layout and of a litre) and the tier of the model (the efficiency of the tier). The factory engine of a car is the one of its definition; an engine part replaces it. An engine goes into the bay of the body only when the layout is allowed and the displacement is not over what the bay holds.

tier_efficiency_ppm_per_tier.description: The power of a litre is grown by this much for every tier above the first (75000: 1 + 0.075 x (tier - 1)), for the engines of the cars and for the engine parts alike.

base_mass_kg.description: What the layout weighs with no litre in it.

bays.description: By the class of the body: the layouts it takes and the displacement it holds at the most.

drivetrain.description: What the drive of a car does (Katalog aut, Napęd): the numbers of the design, one row for each of fwd, rwd and awd. Every factor of a row is taken RELATIVE to the row of `reference`, because the anchors of the design give the front wheel drive starter its base lap: a car with the reference drive is not touched at all (below its power limit), and the others are faster or slower than it by the ratio of the rows. The power limit is absolute: a drive that cannot put more than `kw` on the road loses (kw / power) ^ exponent of the acceleration.

garage.description: The garages of the cities: every one holds a number of cars, which drive on the track of the city by themselves. The first is the one of the home city, and the others are bought. A car without a garage has nowhere to stand.

capacity.description: How many cars a garage holds (the board of the garage says 2 of 3).

price_cents.description: The price of a garage in a city other than the home city.

wreck_price_cents.description: What a wreck costs in the yard of a city, by the slug of the car: its market value, which the first one given by the mentor is not charged.

wreck_mileage_km.description: What the odometer of a wreck says, by the slug of the car (the board of the wrecks: 220 000 to 300 000 km). A wreck has its first service due in the interval of the service after it.

market.description: The markets of the cities (Systemy III, point 11): the used-car exchange, where a car has a hidden condition that an inspection reveals, and the formula that prices a used car. The dealer sells the cars of the pack at their price, and the yard the wrecks of the garage rules.

refresh_ms.description: How long a set of listings lasts before the exchange is refreshed (about 30 minutes).

listings.description: How many cars are on the exchange at a time.

km_per_year.description: How many km a year a car was driven: the age follows from it and the mileage.

age_years.description: The age of a listed car is kept within this.

defect_ppm.description: What one defect takes from the condition of a car, from the least to the most.

defects.description: How many defects a car has, by its mileage: the weights of 0, 1, 2... defects, for the first band the mileage fits in. The weight of 0 is the chance of a car in a perfect condition.

description.description: The word on a listing (good, fair, poor) comes from the condition and a random error, so it only roughly tells the truth.

noise_ppm.description: The error of the word, up or down.

inspection_ppm.description: What an inspection costs, of the price of the car (about 3%).

pricing.description: price = new price * max(floor of the class, age_kept ^ age) * mileage factor * (condition_base + (1 - condition_base) * condition), the formula of Systemy V, point 16.

age_kept_ppm.description: What a car keeps of its value every year.

class_floor_ppm.description: The least a car of a class is worth, of its price new: a collector's car does not fall to nothing.

mileage_per_year_km.description: The mileage that a year of age explains: only the km above it count against the price.

mileage_span_km.description: Over this many km above the norm the car loses its whole mileage factor.

mileage_floor_ppm.description: The mileage factor is never lower than this.

condition_base_ppm.description: A car in no condition at all is worth this much of what it would be in a perfect one.

dealer_mileage_km.description: What the odometer of a new car of the dealer says (the board: 0 to 15 km).

resale_ppm.description: What a driver is paid for a car: this share of its value, as it was when the driver got it (the economy model has 70%).

scrap_cents_per_kg.description: The least a car is bought for, by the kilogram of its mass: what it is worth as scrap.

storage.description: The storage units of the city: a locked unit with a random car in it. The odds are shown before the purchase, the draw is made by the server, and the unit gives at least a good car now and then (the guarantee).

pity_every.description: A unit of a kind that has not given a good car or better this many times in a row gives one the next time.

classes.description: What can be in a unit: scrap, junk, good, and gem. The car has an age, a mileage and a condition within these ranges, and its value is the one of the formula of the exchange.

units.description: The kinds of unit, by key.

unlock_level.description: The level of the driver that opens this kind of unit.

pool_level.description: The cars that can be in it are the ones of the pack that ask this level of a driver or less, so that what is in a unit does not grow with the level of the driver.

odds.description: The weights of scrap, junk, good and gem.

gem_value_cap_cents.description: A gem is worth no more than this (a small unit does not skip the ladder of cars).

start.description: The first car of a driver waits in the garage until the Start of the tournament screen. It leaves with a head start, so that the first lap, which the tutorial waits for, is short.

head_start_ms.description: How much of its first lap the car has driven already when it is sent out. It is never more than the shortest lap of the car less a second.

clock.description: The clock of the game: three real hours are a day of the game (Systemy II). Only the night changes the laps.

night_lap_ppm.description: The lap of a track that is not lit takes this much of its time at night (1 030 000 is 3% longer).

player.description: The level of a driver, from the experience that every lap pays. It opens the tracks, and the cities, one after the other. The first levels are the table early_xp (the experience that reaches level 2, 3, ...), so that the first hour is quick; from the catch-up level on the experience that reaches level n is xp_base * n ^ xp_exponent, rounded, and the levels between are on a straight line from the end of the table to that curve.

other_cars_xp_ppm.description: How much of the experience of the laps of a car that the driver does not play goes to the driver (ppm): 0 is none, 1 000 000 is all of it. The car that is played gives all of it. A fleet of parked cars still earns cash and levels its own cars, but does not level the driver (the economy model's `model.fleet.other_cars_xp_share` has to say the same).

early_xp.description: The experience that reaches level 2, 3, ... in all: rising.

catch_up_level.description: The level from which the curve is the plain one: it has to be above the last level of the table.

shop.description: What the shop of the city sells. Without rarity every part has the price of its definition.

parts.description: Slugs of the parts for sale, all in the core pack.

rarity_stat_ppm.description: What a part of each rarity multiplies its statistics by (Systemy I): 1 000 000 is none. Only what a part adds to a car is multiplied (grip, handling, braking, clearance, and the gain of power), not a limit like the one of a gearbox.

crates.description: The crates of the shop: one draw of a part of a rarity, for game cash only. The odds are shown before the purchase, the draw is made by the server, every one is written down, and the guarantees give a rarer part now and then.

slots.description: The slots a crate draws parts for: the other parts of the shop (the engine group) are only sold, because the pool of a crate is made of the parts of the shop and its price is their mean.

first_tier_level.description: The player level that opens the crates of tier 1.

levels_per_tier.description: Every further tier opens this many levels later: tier t opens at max(first_tier_level, levels_per_tier * (t - 1)), as the cars of the dealer do.

tier_price_ppm.description: A factor on the price of a crate, from a tier on (ppm, 1 000 000 is none): the factor of a tier is the one of the highest tier named that is at most it. The tiers have to name tier 1. A crate of a high tier would pay back sooner than the next car of the ladder, so it costs a little more (the economy simulator checks it).

odds.description: The weights of the rarities, per mille, for each group of crates.

guarantee.description: What every group of crates gives now and then, counted over the openings of the whole group.

kinds.description: The kinds of crate, by key: what group they draw from, what they cost (a share of the mean price of the models they can give, in ppm), the player level that opens them, and whether the driver chooses the slot.

affixes.description: The bonuses that a part above common has (Systemy I), drawn once when the part gets its rarity and kept: how many a rarity gives, and what an affix is. A part never has the same affix twice. An affix changes one thing: a statistic of the part (stat), how fast the part wears (wear), how much fuel the car burns (fuel), or how likely the car is to break down (reliability). The amount is drawn between min_ppm and max_ppm, in ppm.

per_rarity.description: How many affixes a part gets when it is made of that rarity, drawn between min and max. A part that is merged up keeps the ones it has and gets the ones it lacks; a rarity gives more affixes, not bigger ones.

workshop.description: Jobs of the workshop: putting a part on a car and taking it off. One mechanic, and no equipment yet, so a job takes base_time_ms of the slot times the tier, cut by the level of the mechanic.

time_cut_ppm_per_level.description: How much of the time every level of the mechanic cuts.

removal_ppm.description: Taking a part off takes this share of the time of putting it on.

max_queue.description: How many jobs can wait in the queue of a workshop that has one mechanic at work, the one that is done included.

queue_per_extra_worker.description: How many more jobs fit in the queue for every mechanic at work after the first (a mechanic works when he has a bay).

bays.description: The bays of a workshop (Systemy III, point 9): how many cars are worked on at once. The first one is there from the start. price_cents[n] is what the bay number n+1 costs, bought one after the other.

mechanics.description: The mechanics of a workshop: how many work at once, as far as there are bays for them (workers = min(mechanics, bays)). The first one is there from the start. price_cents[n] is what the mechanic number n+1 costs, bought one after the other.

equipment.description: The equipment of a workshop, per city (Systemy III, point 9): every item has levels, bought one after the other, and the level it has multiplies the time of a job by time_ppm (level 0 is the start state, 1000000 = the times of the rules). The tire machine, the lift and the hoist speed up the jobs on the parts of their slots (putting on, taking off, upgrading and repairing); the toolkit speeds up every job, merging and the service included. A level can ask a fee of every job it speeds up (the vulcanizer outside the workshop).

upgrade.description: Upgrading a part to +N (Systemy II, point 7): the statistics of a part are the ones of the model times the rarity times (1 + stat_ppm_per_level * N), and the step from +n to +n+1 costs cost_ppm_of_price * cost_growth_ppm ^ n of the price of the model and takes base_time_ms * time_growth_ppm ^ n (cut by the level of the mechanic, like any job). How far a part goes is limited by its rarity (max_by_rarity) and by the level of the car (car.levels_per_upgrade).

merge.description: Merging two parts (Systemy I, point 3): two parts of one slot, tier and rarity that are not on a car make one part of the next rarity, or fail and are lost. The chance of the attempt that makes the rarity r is base_ppm[r] + level_ppm for every level of the mechanic (the level of the workshop) + pity_ppm for every failure since the last success at that slot and rarity, and at most max_ppm. An attempt costs cost_ppm_of_price of the price of the model, takes time_ppm_of_mount of the time of putting that part on (cut by the mechanic), and when it fails the driver gets scrap_ppm_of_price of the price of the model back.

base_time_ms.description: Time of putting on a part of tier 1, per slot. A part of tier T takes T times as long.

tire_matrix.description: How well every kind of tires grips on every surface, in ppm: the grip, the handling and the braking of a car are multiplied by it. The one tire that is best on every surface does not exist.

weather.description: Effect of every weather. The ground says which surface of the track it makes (dry, wet or snow); statistics are multiplied by stat_ppm / 1 000 000 on top of the tire matrix, the lap reward and XP by reward_ppm and xp_ppm.

name.description: The name of the city of this region, as the map shows it.

map.description: Where the city is on the map, in the 390 by 716 units of the board (Mapa).

weather_ppm.description: Chance of every weather in a 22.5 minute segment, adding up to 1 000 000.

roads.description: The roads between the cities (the regions): a car travels along them, and the way is the shortest one.

travel.description: What a journey costs a car: it drives a share of its top speed on average, and burns fuel by the kilometre (times the thirst of the car).

speed_share_ppm.description: The average speed on the road as a share of the top speed of the car.

fuel_ml_per_km.description: The fuel of a kilometre for a car of the thirst of the track fuel use (1.0).

surface.description: What the track is made of when it is dry. The weather turns it wet or snowy.

reference_tires.description: The tires of the car that the bots of the race are made around, when the stock tires are not what the track asks for: on gravel every stock car is a second slower than a car with the right tires, and a field made around the stock ones would pay a bonus to everyone who buys them. Without it the reference car has the stock tires.

lit.description: Whether the track has lights: a track that has none takes longer to drive at night.

min_player_level.description: The level of the driver from which the track is open. A car is thought of as the level of the track when the tracks are compared: it can mount the tier that level reaches.

base_lap_ms.description: Lap time of a car that matches the reference exactly.

length_m.description: How long a lap is, in metres: what the odometer of a car and the wear of its parts grow by with every lap.

xp_per_lap.description: The XP of a lap of the base time, in dry weather. A car that laps faster gets the share of it that its lap is of the base lap, so that an hour on the track gives every car the same XP: XP is for the time of driving, and a faster car only drives more laps. A car that is slower gets all of it.

demand.description: How much every statistic counts on this track, in percent, adding up to 100.

reference.description: The value of a statistic that counts as normal on this track.

purchase_prices.description: What the next one costs, by how many there are already: the first is free (it is there from the start), and every price is higher than the one before.

time_ppm.description: What the time of a job is multiplied by.

price_cents.description: What it costs to get this level from the one before (0 for the start state).

fee_cents.description: What a job it speeds up costs while this is the level that is there (the work done outside).

crateOdds.description: The weights of the five rarities of a part (any scale; the odds are shown in percent of their sum).

every.description: A crate of the group that follows this many minus one without a part of the rarity below, or better, gives one (the 10th of 10).

legendary_every.description: A crate that follows this many minus one without a legendary part gives one.

surfaces.description: A multiplier for each surface a car can drive on: dry asphalt, wet asphalt, dry gravel, mud (wet gravel) and snow.

drivetrain.description: One drive. The factors multiply the car (1 000 000 is neutral): `start_ppm` the acceleration, `handling_ppm` the handling, `mass_penalty_ppm` both of them, `fuel_ppm` the fuel use, `service_ppm` the price of a service; `traction_ppm` multiplies the grip, the handling and the braking on each surface, like the tire matrix. `power_limit` is optional: above `kw` the acceleration is multiplied by (kw / power) ^ exponent.

affix.description: One kind of affix. stat is the statistic that a stat affix multiplies by 1 + the amount (power is the power of the engine, or the gain of a part that adds power); wear, fuel and reliability take the amount off how fast the part wears, how much fuel the car burns and how likely it is to break down.

weight.description: How often it is drawn among the affixes that fit the slot.
